findings.title: TECH-SPEC §6.x / DECISIONS-r3 Q8 'one fixed default timeout' re-breaks the exact fix shipped for v1 #406
findings.claim_reopened: TECH-SPEC.md:437 says: 'ctx_execute: one fixed default timeout, value set by measurement (not 120 s, v1 #406)'. DECISIONS-r3.md Q8 cites commit v1 #406 as the source for this rule.
findings.evidence: git log shows commit eea5877b (v1, 'Mickey 3-issue + Issue #406 timeout policy') DID THE OPPOSITE: it dropped the Zod `.default(30000)`/`.default(60000)` from ctx_execute/ctx_execute_file/ctx_batch_execute entirely, and changed PolyglotExecutor so that when timeout is undefined NO setTimeout timer is set at all. Commit message states explicitly: 'Server-side timeout policy is the wrong layer — every MCP host already enforces its own RPC timeout — and stacking env-var defaults on top would create dead config.' This was done because long Gradle/Maven/SBT builds were being killed by the old fixed/default timeout.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: eea5877b 2026-05-03 'fix(opencode-plugin+executor+routing): Mickey 3-issue + Issue #406 timeout policy' (v1 issue #406, reporter @wax911). ORIGINAL_INTENT (quoted from commit body): 'Long-running build commands (Gradle/Maven/SBT) were terminated by the Zod .default(30000) ms timeout ... whenever the caller forgot to pass an explicit value. Server-side timeout policy is the wrong layer ... Fix: Drop the Zod .default(...) from all three tools' timeout schemas; keep .optional(). When the caller omits timeout, no server-side timer fires.' REGRESSION_RISK: if v2 ships ANY always-on default timeout (even one 'set by measurement' instead of hardcoded 120s), long builds (gradle/mvn/sbt) that the deny-with-alternative in ADR-0008 explicitly routes into ctx_execute will again be killed mid-build, reopening #406 for exactly the golden case ADR-0008 lists ('./gradlew build -> deny; the alternative has no tail'). SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: either (a) keep ctx_execute's timeout optional with no server-side default, consistent with v1's actual fix, and only measure/bound sub-cases that are known-bounded (e.g. batch's own default), or (b) if the owner genuinely wants a new default, the doc must say so as a deliberate reversal of #406's intent, not as if #406 supports it.
findings.fix: Correct TECH-SPEC.md:437 and DECISIONS-r3 Q8: either state that ctx_execute timeout stays optional/no-default (matching #406's actual fix) and drop the 'one fixed default timeout, v1 #406' framing, or explicitly flag this as reopening #406 and get a owner decision that overrides it on the record.

findings.title: Q3 / ADR-0016 case B citation of v1 4bc292fc is accurate (re-verified, not a finding)
findings.claim_reopened: DECISIONS-r3 Q3 / ADR-0016 case B: 'allow + updatedInput is never used, because Claude Code ignores it for Bash (v1 4bc292fc)'
findings.evidence: git show 4bc292fc confirms: 'fix(hooks): claude-code Bash modify -> deny (CC ignores updatedInput.command)' — commit body: 'CC v2.1.x Bash tool ignores updatedInput.command substitution under permissionDecision:"allow" — the original command runs unchanged. Only permissionDecision:"deny" is honored for Bash blocking.' This matches the doc claim exactly.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: 4bc292fc 2026-05-31. ORIGINAL_INTENT: fix a high-impact regression where curl/wget redirects silently no-op'd. REGRESSION_RISK: none identified for this citation. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: n/a.
findings.fix: No doc change needed; listed to show the claim was re-opened and checked, not skipped.
